Question: Menkara has a \(4 \times 6\) index card. If she shortens the length of one side of this card by \(1\) inch, the card would have area \(18\) square inches. What would the area of the card be in square inches if instead she shortens the length of the other side by \(1\) inch?
Solution:
Shortening a side changes one dimension of the rectangle. Starting with a \(4\)-inch by \(6\)-inch card, the two possible new dimensions are \(3\) by \(6\), or \(4\) by \(5\).

Their areas are \(18\) and \(20\) square inches. Since the first shortening gives \(18\), shortening the other side gives \(\boxed{20}\) square inches, choice E.
